findings.description: Design D2 calls roadmap/checkpoint terminal-status disagreement both a normal short-lived ordering mismatch and an inconsistent workspace that is withheld. That conflicts with the normative scenario requiring a valid checkpoint completion to unblock external dependents while roadmap status still lags.
findings.resolution: Separate hard-invalid checkpoint conditions, which withhold the workspace, from soft roadmap/checkpoint status divergence, which sets stale and emits a diagnostic while preserving checkpoint-authoritative readiness and completion.

findings.description: Design D5 promises deterministic diagnostics and non-zero exit for malformed canonical input, but the JSON contract has no bounded diagnostic codes for an invalid roadmap or duplicate roadmap_id; only checkpoint failures are representable.
findings.resolution: Add roadmap_invalid and duplicate_roadmap_id codes and specify that both are hard-invalid workspace conditions with non-zero CLI status.

findings.description: The phrase 'canonical serialization of every readiness-relevant input' does not enumerate normalized fields, ordering, missing-checkpoint sentinel, or malformed-input fallback. Two conforming implementations could generate different fingerprints for identical semantic state.
findings.resolution: Define the exact normalized roadmap/checkpoint projection, list ordering, path identity, absent-checkpoint sentinel, and raw-byte digest fallback for malformed input.

findings.description: The one-package sequential DAG is appropriate because moving the admission helper, adding repository aggregation, and switching the supervisor consumer all touch one authority boundary and must remain green together.
findings.resolution: No change; keep the single package and explicit file locks.
